messages.subject: uiOutput or renderUI block JavaScript?
parts:
Hi, 
    I am writing a JavaScript to track user's operation on my app. It works using regular inputs: 

     runGist("https://gist.github.com/withr/8434843")

    However, if I use "renderUI", it will not work. 

    runGist("https://gist.github.com/withr/8434907")

I noted that "renderUI" is an "Experimental feature", so maybe this is bug of it? However, I really like use "renderUI"  to dynamically generate inputs.
Any suggest are highly appreciated!

Regards!

messages.subject: Re: uiOutput or renderUI block JavaScript?
parts:
I know nothing about this, but I found the idea intriguing. Your demos are very useful to have. A wild guess, might it be related to this issue:

Joe Cheng:

The problem isn't in the reactivity; if you set "options(shiny.trace=TRUE)" you can see that when you click the button, the value is going to the server ("RECV"); and that the server replies back with the HTML for textbox ("SEND"). Yet nothing actually changes on the client.

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!msg/shiny-discuss/PLHauRlFw3k/AnoD7NusvDIJ

messages.author: b949e0841d7e094b
messages.subject: Re: uiOutput or renderUI block JavaScript?
parts:
The same issue but more detailed and with workaround:

Winston Chang:

The value field of the element doesn't change when the user types in the box. When the HTML code is re-sent to the browser, Shiny doesn't bother updating the object since the HTML code is exactly the same.

https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/308

messages.subject: Re: uiOutput or renderUI block JavaScript?
parts:
Huidong, the problem is that at the time that the inputTracking.js code runs, the controls you want aren't part of the page yet. This is a common problem in jQuery, the solution is to use delegated events (scroll down to the section entitled "Direct and delegated events" and read it carefully).

I've created a fork for you that demonstrates this, as well as simplifying the event handling logic:

https://gist.github.com/jcheng5/8441665
